messages.author: c3e53d7d5317214f
messages.subject: CDF of the t-distribution
parts:
Hi,

I want to use the skew t-distribution which is defined in terms of the PDF and CDF of the t-distribution. However, I've found that there is no AD implementation of the CDF.

As far as I'm concerned, the building blocks like the Gamma function seem to be there (as this is needed for dt or dgamma). So is it possible to somewhat easily define an AD version of pt myself?

Cheers,
Ole

messages.author: c3e53d7d5317214f
messages.subject: Re: CDF of the t-distribution
parts:
Actually, I found a pretty simple way to implement it using the definition on Wikipedia.

However, this is only for q>0, but can easily be extended by symmetry. 
But this poses a problem when q is an ad type as I cannot use comparisons. 

Of course, this function is actually continuous and differentiable so it shouldn't pose a problem in theory. 
But as mentioned, in the practical implementation below I face the issue of comparing ad types.

Is there a simple way around this?

pt_ad = function(q, df){
  x = df / (df + q^2)
 
  pos_ind = which(q => 0)
  neg_ind = which(q < 0)
 
  CDF = numeric(length(q))
 
  CDF[pos_ind] = 1 - 0.5 * RTMB::pbeta(x[pos_ind], df/2, 0.5) # definition for q >= 0
  CDF[neg_ind] = 0.5 * RTMB::pbeta(x[neg_ind], df/2, 0.5) # for q < 0: 1- the above
 
  return(CDF)
}

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: CDF of the t-distribution
parts:
Based on an earlier post  https://groups.google.com/g/tmb-users/c/wOR02nMigdg/m/SlbsjkxqAwAJ  on this list, a first shot could be:

pt <- function(x, df) {
    nx <- 1 + (x/df)*x
    val <- pbeta (1. / nx, df / 2., 0.5)
    val <- val / 2
    test <- .5 * (sign(x) + 1)  ## x>0
    test * (1-val) + (1-test) * val
}

which seems to work

F <- MakeTape(function(x)pt(x[1],x[2]),1:2)
F(3:4)
[1] 0.980029
stats::pt(3,4)
[1] 0.980029

but it should probably be checked more thoroughly.
